Neeraj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 45530 of 2024
Applicant :- Neeraj

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Kapil Dev Dubey,Pratikdhar Dwivedi,Rahul Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Pratikdhar Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned
Aga-I for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
147 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Lalauli, District Fatehpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 28.7.2024 against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant on 4.5.2019 and after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured her for additional demand of motorcycle and golden chain and due to their torture for demand of dowry on 1.6.2024 she committed suicide by hanging herself.
4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture he has been made accused in the present matter alongwith his family members.
Neeraj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17038952/
1 5.

He further submitted that admittedly deceased committed suicide on 1.6.2024 but FIR of the present case was lodged on 28.7.2024 i.e. after about two months and this inordinate delay in lodging the FIR itself suggests that FIR of the present case is based on false and fabricated facts and actually it is not a case of dowry death.
6.

He further submitted that actually on the date of incident applicant was not present at his home and it appears behind him some dispute of the deceased arose with some one and thereafter in haste and anger she hanged herself.
7. He further submitted that post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
8. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 8.8.2024.

9. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within five and half years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after about two months and post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within five and half years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and torture but FIR of the present case was lodged after about two months and no plausible explanation has been given by the informant in this regard and therefore, there is inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.

12. Further, post mortem report of the deceased suggests that deceased died due to hanging,
therefore, prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.
13. Further, applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 8.8.2024.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant- Neeraj, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Neeraj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17038952/
2
( i ) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 12.12.2024 Ankita  Neeraj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17038952/
